answer: One concrete defense is stake-bonded identity: each agent must lock a scarce, slashable deposit before its attestations count, and rewards accrue along a single verifiable thread of history. Creating a thousand sybils needs a thousand independently funded bonds, plus the cost of maintaining separate auditable histories. Any agent caught fabricating has its deposit burned, so the attacker pays capital per identity instead of amortizing one fee across a nebula of fakes. Like timber, trust is grown grain by grain and cannot be cloned overnight; the ledger makes forgery costlier than honest work.
